newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares reached another record close on Monday, with the continuing strength of Wall Street and a stronger dollar as main supportive elements.
The AEX share index rose 6.89 points to 652.84. Dealers said the index was not expected to show big moves in the near-term, but some said a moderate correction could come within weeks.

Vendex jumped to a new record close in heavy volume after the firm announced it was buying French employment agency BIS for 490 French francs per share. Vendex stock closed five guilders higher at 81.80 guilders.
The Midcap index of medium-sized firms, which includes Vendex, rose almost 1.5 percent to 972.10 points, while the main AEX-index gained just over one percent.

Office equipment group Ahrend and supermarkets group De Boer Winkelbedrijven also boosted the Midcap index. De Boer announced earlier on Monday that its 1996 turnover had increased by over 25 percent.
Financials were very strong, with ING, Aegon and Fortis Amev peaking. ING added 1.10 guilders to 63.70.
One dealer said ABN AMRO, rising 1.30 guilders to 111.90, was likely to gain further.
He said the market would become bullish about ABN's full-year 1996 results, due on February 27.
"Expectations are good. The market will soon start speculating on the outcome," he said.
Brewer Heineken, to announce its expansion strategy after the bourse closed, was 5.60 guilders higher at 312.00.

Dealers said many private investors were looking at last year's underperformers in the hope they would make up for their losses. Once such stock, of sanitary maker Sphinx, rose 1.60 guilders to 23.40.
"I do not expect much profit from the firm," said one dealer, adding investors should remain cautious with Sphinx.
He added that Dutch shares should show a modest downside correction within the next few weeks in response to record-breaking sessions to date.
"But there is a lot of liquidity around, so the dip won't be strong and that will also be the moment that many big institutions will jump back into the market," he said.
Other stocks recovering strongly were Axxicon and Toolex.
Akzo Nobel, publisher VNU and tank storage firm Pakhoed were strong performers among the bigger stocks.
